item.title: DW745 Mobile Saw Cart (Proposed)
item.description:
A proposed build: a small plywood cart on locking casters for a DeWalt DW745 10" jobsite table saw. It’s deliberately compact. The footprint is just over the saw’s table, it comes out of one sheet of plywood, and it holds the saw’s accessories underneath. The saw comes off with four knobs when it needs to go to a jobsite.

  • Footprint: 28" W × 24" D. The DW745’s table is about 630 × 570 mm (24.8" × 22.4"), so the cart is just over 1" bigger on each side.
  • Saw table height: 34" from the floor, a standard bench height, so a workbench can serve as outfeed. Some shops prefer ~35.5" (900 mm); pick yours and plug it into the formula below.
  • Casters: 4 of my step-stop locking casters, one at each corner.
  • Material: ¾" plywood (birch or good-one-side), glue and screws.
 .--------------------------------------.
| DW745 table (34″) |
'----+----------------------------+----'
| saw body |
| s = base to table top |
+------------+----------------------------+------------+ cart top
| |
| upper bay: push sticks, wrenches, blade guard |
+------------------------------------------------------+ shelf
| |
| lower bay: blades, dust bag, heavy items |
+------------------------------------------------------+ bottom
(o) (o) c = caster
=========================================================== floor
|<----------------------- 28″ ----------------------->|

Set the height first

Two measurements decide the carcass height. Take them before cutting anything:

  1. s: from the bottom of the saw’s base (where it’ll sit on the cart) to the top of the saw table.
  2. c: from the caster’s mounting plate to the floor.

Carcass height H = 34" − s − c. That’s the outside height of the box, top and bottom panels included.

Example (yours will differ) s c H Interior (H − 1½")
3" casters 13.5" 3.5" 17" 15.5"
4" casters 13.5" 4.5" 16" 14.5"
5" casters 13.5" 5.5" 15" 13.5"

The s = 13.5" here is only a placeholder; I don’t have a published base-to-table height for the DW745. Measure your saw.

Cut list (one 4×8 sheet of ¾" plywood)

Cut sizes for the example H = 16" (interior 14.5"). If your H is different, change the 14.5" dimensions to match your interior height.

Part Qty Size Notes
Top 1 28" × 24" Saw mounts here
Bottom 1 28" × 24" Casters mount here
Sides 2 14.5" × 24" Captured between top and bottom
Back 1 14.5" × 26.5" Between the sides; squares and stiffens the box
Shelf 1 26.5" × 22.75" Set 1" back from the front edge, at mid-height

That’s about 22 ft² of the sheet’s 32 ft². The offcut is enough for push sticks and a cord cleat.

Hardware

Qty Item Use
4 Step-stop locking casters (on hand) one per corner, plates flush to the corners
16 5/16" carriage bolts, 1½", with washers and nylock nuts through-bolt the caster plates; match your plate holes
4 ¼"-20 T-nuts in the top, under the saw’s base mounting holes
4 ¼"-20 star knobs (2" studs) + fender washers hold the saw down; removable without tools
~40 1⅝" coarse wood screws carcass
— Wood glue, edge banding (optional)
2 Cord cleats or hooks (offcut) on one side, for the cord

Build

  1. Box: glue and screw the sides to the bottom, then add the back between the sides. Check that it’s square, then add the top. Fit the shelf on cleats or dados at mid-height.
  2. Casters: bolt one under each corner of the bottom, plates as close to the corners as they’ll go. A wider wheelbase means a less tippy cart.
  3. Saw mount: set the saw centered on the top, with the blade parallel to the cart’s sides, and mark its base mounting holes through from above. Drill and install the ¼"-20 T-nuts from underneath, then hold the saw down with the four knobs.
  4. Finish: ease the edges and give it a coat of wipe-on poly or paste wax so sawdust doesn’t stick.

Using it safely

  • Lock all four casters before you turn the saw on. Step-stop casters that lock both the wheel and the swivel are what you want. A cart that creeps during a rip is a kickback risk.
  • Keep heavy items on the bottom shelf. The saw makes the cart top-heavy, and weight down low keeps it planted.
  • Support long stock. On a footprint this small, don’t rip sheet goods or long boards without infeed and outfeed support. At 34" a workbench or roller stand works.
  • Keep the rear dust port clear, and run a shop-vac hose off the back instead of through the cart.

Buy instead?

DeWalt makes rolling stands for this saw, the DE7400 wheeled stand and the DW7451 compact stand. They fold, they’re quick, and they cost more than this cart. They’re the better choice if the saw travels a lot. This cart wins in the shop, with storage, a solid base, and casters you already own.
